title: SRE documentation standards: SLOs, error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, and runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines Redwood Inference SRE standards for writing and maintaining SLOs and error budgets, running capacity planning, coordinating reliability initiatives, conducting incident reviews, and authoring operational runbooks. The goal is consistent, actionable documentation that enables predictable service behavior and fast incident resolution.

Scope:
Applies to all customer-facing inference services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, private control plane) and supporting platform services (routing, cache, queuing, billing).

Audience:
SREs, service owners, product engineers, platform engineers, and engineering managers.

---

1) SLO and Error Budget Standards

SLO naming and intent
- SLOs must be customer-centric: measure user-visible correctness, availability, latency, or quality (e.g., generation latency, request success, embedding correctness).
- Name format: <service>-<metric>-<window>-<objective> (example: api-generate-success-rate-30d-99.95%).

SLO-eligible metrics (recommended):
- Availability / success rate: percentage of requests that complete successfully (HTTP 2xx + semantic validation).
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for latency-critical endpoints (token generation p95).
- Throughput: sustained QPS for throughput contracts (Dedicated reservations).
- Correctness / quality: model-specific eval pass rate on production prompt sets (where applicable).

Example SLO table:
| SLO id | Service | Metric | Window | Objective | Rationale | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| SLO-A1 | hosted-api/generate | success rate | 30d | 99.95% | Primary customer-facing API availability | api-platform-owner@redwood.com |
| SLO-A2 | hosted-api/generate | latency (p95) | 30d | <150ms | User interactive generation target | runtime-performance@redwood.com |
| SLO-B1 | embeddings | success rate | 30d | 99.99% | High throughput embedding batches | embeddings-team@redwood.com |

Error budget policy (standard):
- Error budget = 1 - objective. Track burn daily and rolling 30-day.
- Actions by burn level (30d):
  1. <10% burn: normal operations.
  2. 10% - 30% burn: service owner notified; deprioritize large non-essential changes.
  3. 30% - 50% burn: require a mitigation plan within 48h; pause non-essential launches.
  4. 50% - 75% burn: mandatory canary rollback for risky changes; increase monitoring cadence; oncall pager may trigger.
  5. >75% burn: emergency incident review; freeze deploys for the service; exec notification and cross-team war room.
- If budget is exhausted: schedule a post-incident reliability initiative and update capacity/rollout plans.

SLO definition template (required fields):
- title (string)
- id (slug)
- service(s) covered
- metric definition (precise query, accepted error cases)
- measurement window (rolling 30d default)
- objective (e.g., 99.95%)
- rationale (business impact)
- owner (primary + secondary)
- alerting thresholds and runbook link
- last_reviewed_date

---

2) Capacity Planning Standards

Goals:
- Ensure predictable capacity for customer-facing SLAs and Dedicated reservations.
- Maintain >20% headroom for burst tolerant services by default, configurable by service class.

Quarterly planning cadence:
1. Forecasting (collaboration between product, SRE, infra finance): ingest historical QPS, per-model token cost, runway for reserved capacity, and expected product changes.
2. Baseline requirement: compute steady-state GPU/CPU and network/resource utilization for 95th percentile load.
3. Headroom policy: add at least 20% headroom for hosted API; Dedicated capacity follows contract.
4. Procurement / scaling runbook: autoscale policy review, reserved capacity purchase requests, and on-call simulated failover tests.

Capacity playbook checklist:
- Data sources: Datadog metrics, request logs, model token distribution, KV cache hit rates, and queue lengths.
- Run a capacity simulation monthly for top-10 customers and a 99th percentile traffic spike scenario.
- Validate autoscaler behavior in staging and canary; include scale-down cooldowns to avoid flapping.

---

3) Reliability Initiatives and Prioritization

Initiative types:
- Technical debt reduction (e.g., replacing brittle retry logic)
- Observability improvements (additional metrics, tracing, SLI coverage)
- Architectural changes (sharding, dedicated routing pools)

Prioritization rubric (impact / effort):
- Impact: reduced customer pain, error budget recovery, cost optimization.
- Effort: engineering hours and required infra spend.
- Expected ROI: measurable SLO uplift or cost savings within 3 months.

Process:
1. Proposal: owner fills RFC with SLO impact estimate and test plan.
2. Triage in monthly reliability review meeting; assign priority and timeframe.
3. Delivery: include metrics to validate success and a rollback plan.
4. Post-delivery: track impact on SLOs and error budgets for 30-90 days.

---

4) Incident Review Standards

Purpose: produce blameless, actionable post-incident reviews that drive improvement.

Incident review checklist:
- Summary (what happened, timeline)
- Impact (customers affected, SLOs impacted, error budget consumed)
- Root cause analysis (5 whys)
- Detection and response timeline (detection time, mitigation time)
- Mitigations applied and their effectiveness
- Action items (owner, due date, verification steps)
- Communications effectiveness and customer outreach notes

Severity mapping and review cadence:
- Sev3: internal postmortem optional; runbook update recommended.
- Sev2: mandatory post-incident review in 7 days; assign action items.
- Sev1 / P1: executive postmortem within 72 hours; remediation plan and follow-up audits.

Inclusion criteria for a full RCA:
- >10% customer impact or >20% error budget burn in 30d or more than 1 hour of degraded service.

Template location: link to runbook SRE postmortem template (see runbook section link).

---

5) Operational Tooling and Ownership

Core tools (standardized):
- Metrics / dashboards: Datadog (primary), Grafana (internal aggregated views)
- Alerting: PagerDuty for paging; Slack for informational alerts and runbook links
- Tracing: Jaeger / OpenTelemetry for cross-service traces
- Logs: centralized ELK / Loki with retained indexes for 90 days by default (longer on request)
- Incident tracking: Jira/Confluence linked postmortems and action tracking

Owner responsibilities:
- SRE Tooling team: maintain and curate shared dashboards, alert runbooks, and escalation policies.
- Service owners: own per-service alerting thresholds and runbooks.

Alert hygiene standards:
- Alerts should be actionable, with runbook link and expected responder.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) targets: <5m for P1, <30m for P2.
- Alert noise reduction: aim for fewer than 5 noise alerts per week for critical channels.

---

6) Runbook Standards and Templates

Runbook minimum fields (flat text at top of page):
- title
- service
- owner(s) + contact
- pager routing
- symptoms (how users/devs will observe the problem)
- quick mitigations (1-3 steps for fast mitigation)
- diagnostics (commands, queries, dashboard links)
- full remediation steps (ordered, tested)
- rollback plan
- post-incident follow-up link (postmortem)

Quick example (excerpt):
- title: hosted-api/generate - high error rate
- symptoms: 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m; p95 latency > 500ms
- quick mitigations:
  1. Scale up inference pool for model-x via infra console (link)
  2. Switch routing policy to fallback-model-x-lightweight (link)
  3. Enable circuit breaker for batch endpoints (CLI snippet: redwoodctl circuit enable batch-ingest)
- diagnostics commands:
  - datadog query: "avg:service.http.errors{service:hosted-api,generation} by {env}"
  - kubectl: describe pods, check GPU utilization and OOM events

Runbook lifecycle:
- Review cadence: every 6 months or after any P1/P2 incident.
- Ownership: must have a primary and secondary owner.
- Testing: runbook dry-runs during game days at least twice per year.

---

7) Governance and Documentation Practices

- Every SLO, error budget, and runbook must be stored in Confluence (space = eng-sre) and referenced in an in-repo service README.
- SLOs and runbooks must include last_reviewed and review schedule metadata.
- Changes to SLO objectives or error budget policy require review by SRE leads and Product (minimum 2 reviewers).

---

Appendix A: Common SLO examples and thresholds
- API availability (hosted-api/generate): 99.95% / 30d
- Latency (hosted-api/generate p95): <150ms / 30d
- Dedicated control plane provisioning time: 99% < 10m (reservation fulfillment)
- KV cache hit rate (runtime cache): >85% sustained

Appendix B: Emergency contacts and escalation matrix
- Primary SRE oncall: see PagerDuty rota (link)
- Platform lead: platform-lead@redwood.com
- Eng manager oncall escalation: eng-mgr-oncall@redwood.com
